description:
fetch_mta_sts_policy_body checks for '://' and '/' in the domain argument but does not check for '@'. In RFC 3986, '@' in the host component of a URL separates userinfo from the actual host. A domain value like 'evil.com@target.com' produces URL 'https://mta-sts.evil.com@target.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt', where the actual TLS connection target is 'target.com' (not 'mta-sts.evil.com'). This allows a crafted domain argument to redirect the policy fetch to an unintended host. The current call site (do_deliver via enforce_for_delivery) derives the domain from rfind('@') on the RCPT address, which limits direct exploitation, but the fetcher function's own guard is incomplete and cannot be trusted in isolation. The domain guard should add '@' to the blocklist.

## Context
mta_sts_fetcher.rs line 32. RFC 3986 §3.2.1: authority component is [userinfo@]host[:port]. A '@' in the domain inserts a userinfo component, changing the effective host.
title: mta_sts_fetcher: '@' character not blocked in domain validation allows URL userinfo injection
